articles.title: Losing Supreme Court Argument? No Problem! — See Also
articles.content:
**当你是巨星**：特朗普对败诉出生公民权案件深感不满。昨日，他颁布行政命令声称自己获胜。

**柯林斯反对，穆尔科斯反对，麦康奈尔缺席。卡西迪：好，没问题。** 托德·布兰奇将成为美国司法部长，但通过率比预期更低。

**华盛顿法考免试来了，但不适用所有人。** 首次参考被拒的考生获免试，而坚持参加破碎考试的人则被困于成绩。

**支付我所欠的**：大型律所律师加薪仍未确定。律所应停止等待克拉瓦特。

**这太疯狂了**：联邦学会联合创始人不懂香蕉如何成熟。

（原文出自《Above the Law》）
articles.summary:
When You’re A Star: Donald Trump bitterly complained about losing the birthright citizenship cases. Yesterday, he issued executive orders asserting that he won.

Collins No. Murkowski No. McConnell Absent. Cassidy: Sure, Fine. Todd Blanche is going to be Attorney General of the United States. but it’s closer than anyone expected.

The Bar Exam Waiver Comes For Washington’s Grads. Just Not All Of Them. First-timers who got shut out are being waived in. The ones who ground through the broken exam are stuck with their scores.

Pay Me What You Owe Me: Raises for Biglaw associates are still MIA. Firms need to stop waiting for Cravath.

This Is Bananas: FedSoc co-founder befuddled by green bananas.

articles.title: The Trial That Made The Supreme Court Untouchable
articles.content:
编辑按：欢迎来到我们的每日特辑今日趣味问答！

谁是唯一一位曾被众议院弹劾的美国最高法院法官？

提示：这位法官是《独立宣言》的签署者，由乔治·华盛顿任命。他因其政治对手指控的公然党派行为而被参议院控告8项罪状。最终他被宣告无罪——这一结果长期以来被认为确立了一个法官不能仅因执政党不喜欢其裁决而被罢免的先例。

答案将在下一页公布。

原文《那场使最高法院不可动摇的审判》首次发表于《法律之上》。
articles.summary:
Ed. Note: Welcome to our daily feature Trivia Question of the Day!

Who is the only Supreme Court justice who has ever been impeached by the House?

Hint: A signer of the Declaration of Independence appointed by George Washington, he was hauled before the Senate on eight articles for conduct his political enemies called nakedly partisan. He was acquitted — an outcome long credited with establishing that a justice can’t be removed simply for rulings the ruling party dislikes.

See the answer on the next page.

articles.title: FedSoc Co-Founder Does Not Understand How Bananas Work
articles.content:
纽约市长马姆达尼近日推出了市立超市计划，设立五家超市，以30%的折扣提供新鲜肉类、蔬菜和食品杂货。这一举措旨在解决"食品沙漠"问题，并理想情况下降低整体食品成本。然而，保守派人士对此反应激烈，连续发出尖叫声反对这一计划。一些自称经济学家的网友声称，以批发价出售商品永远不可行，还拿苏联比喻便宜食品，并讽刺自由派反对选民身份认证却要求购物时出示身份证（实际上这些超市并不需要身份证）。

但最令人印象深刻的回应来自联邦党人协会创始人之一戴维·麦金托什：
"可疑之处，确实存在。"

这些小提醒让我们清楚地看到，尽管保守派常常号召普通美国民众，但真正掌权的保守派仍然不清楚香蕉原本是绿色的，因为他们从未打算了解自己的管家（甚至连管家的名字都不愿记忆），总是小心翼翼地将香蕉从每日水果盘中移除。

然而，2020年，保守派法律运动向我们证明，他们并不懂得如何接受失败。因此，在他的帖子遭到严厉回击后，麦金托什还发布了一个视频，视频中他笨拙地拿起并咬了一口一根从"小超市"（实际上是由他的助手买来的）购得的成熟黄香蕉。

我原想说"把它挂在卢浮宫"，但显然有人已经这么做了。

麦金托什现任哈兰·克劳的"增长俱乐部"主席——是的，就是那个哈兰·克劳——显然他的"增长"愿景并不包括那些寻求负担得起的蔬菜的人。

正如伟大的唐纳德·特朗普曾说：
"一个老式的词汇——杂货。我在竞选时使用过它。这是一个古老的词汇，但也是一个美好的词汇。杂货。它指的是一个装有各种物品的袋子。"

确实如此，先生！确实如此。

乔·帕特里斯是《Above the Law》的资深编辑和《像律师一样思考》的联合主持人。欢迎提供任何线索、问题或评论。如果您对法律、政治和大学体育新闻感兴趣，可以关注他的推特或Bluesky账号。

本文最初发表于《Above the Law》。
articles.summary:
Mayor Mamdani just unveiled his municipal grocery store initiative, creating five stores offering fresh meat, produce, and pantry staples at a substantial 30 percent discount. It’s part of his plan to tackle food deserts and, ideally, drive down food costs generally. Predictably, conservatives began screeching like banshees over the arrangement. Armchair economists explained why selling products at wholesale prices can never work, comparing cheap food to the Soviet Union, and mocking the fact that liberals oppose voter ID while requiring an ID to buy groceries (the stores do not, in fact, require an ID).

But arguably the most impressive response came from Federalist Society co-founder David McIntosh:

Suspicious, indeed.

It’s nice to have these little reminders that, for all the appeals to everyday Americans, the real conservatives running the show still don’t know that the bananas have ever been green because the butler (whose name they’ve never bothered to learn) keeps them tastefully away from the daily fruit bowl display.

Alas, if there’s one thing the conservative legal movement showed us in 2020, it’s that they do not understand how to take an L. In that spirit, McIntosh followed up the brutal ratioing his post received with a video of himself awkwardly holding and then taking a bite out of a properly yellow banana he got (read: an intern got) from a “bodega.”

I’d say “Hang it in the Louvre” but someone already tried that.

McIntosh is currently the president of Harlan Crow’s Club for Growth — yes, that Harlan Crow — and it’s pretty clear his vision of “growth” does not include the people looking for affordable produce.

As the great Donald Trump once said:

An old fashioned term that we use — groceries. I used it on the campaign. It’s such an old fashioned term, but a beautiful term. Groceries. It says a bag with different things in it.

So it does, sir! So it does.

Joe Patrice is a senior editor at Above the Law and co-host of Thinking Like A Lawyer. Feel free to email any tips, questions, or comments. Follow him on Twitter or Bluesky if you’re interested in law, politics, and a healthy dose of college sports news.

articles.title: Todd Blanche Threading The Narrowest Of Needles For Confirmation
articles.content:
今天早晨，参议员丽莎·默科夫斯基宣布她将反对托德·布兰奇的司法部长确认提名，使得路易斯安那州参议员比尔·卡西迪成为唯一一位可能支持布兰奇的共和党议员，这也意味着布兰奇面临着自1989年以来最耻辱的内阁任命失败。

然而，卡西迪似乎没有从罗伯特·F·肯尼迪二世那里学到任何教训。

默科夫斯基发表在X平台上的声明，于清晨6点发布，言辞如往常一样克制而尖锐。她表示布兰奇“看起来是个体面且有能力的人”，赞赏了他对阿拉斯加的访问，并提到一些她认可的决定，但随后写道：“然而，我最终将反对他被提名。司法部的政治化——甚至是武器化——并非始于本届政府，但在本届政府期间加速了。”她提到了爱泼斯坦档案、特朗普及其家人在IRS的豁免权、反武器化基金，以及特朗普政治敌人的针对行为。她写道：“这个国家需要一位司法部长来制衡本届政府的最坏冲动。我希望布兰奇在确认后能够做到这一点，但我简直不抱任何信心。”

随着默科夫斯基和柯林斯都反对，而米奇·麦康奈尔仍因6月份的跌倒事故缺席参议院，布兰奇的提名几乎没有任何余地。于是，焦点转向了卡西迪，这位共和党资深议员在今年早些时候输给了特朗普支持的候选人，并在随后的几个月里表现出越来越多的独立于现任政府的姿态——正是这届政府试图终结他的政治生涯。

尽管如此，卡西迪仍然表示支持。他在星期五早上的演讲中表示：“综合考虑，我将投票支持布兰奇先生。我会因为这张投票受到批评。这有什么新鲜的呢？”

在解释他的投票决定时，卡西迪表示他考虑到了司法部的“武器化”问题，特别是正在进行的对卡西迪·哈奇森的调查，她是前白宫助理和1月6日事件的关键证人，其可能的起诉如同悬在布兰奇确认程序上的达摩克里斯之剑。卡西迪对记者说，他对所谓的“法战”（lawfare）感到担忧，即出于“并非合理原因，而是因为某些高层官员对他们感到愤怒”而进行的起诉。他并非没有认清这是一个问题！……不幸的是，他打算投票支持特朗普最复仇心切的执行者——布兰奇。

我们已经见过这部电影——卡西迪曾被政府戏弄过。他曾在条件性支持罗伯特·F·肯尼迪二世的提名时提出了关于疫苗的具体承诺，但肯尼迪在确认后几乎立即打破了这些承诺，解散了CDC的疫苗咨询委员会，削减了疫苗资金，并在CDC网站上添加了没有根据的内容，质疑疫苗的安全性。现在，卡西迪要投票支持托德·布兰奇，他在书面确认回复中称两位参议员为骗子，在听证会上自我介绍为特朗普的律师，拒绝在书面上承诺以任何有意义的方式保持“政治保护基金”死亡，并在过去的18个月里证明了他的首要忠诚对象是特朗普本人。

布兰奇现在几乎肯定会在参议院进入五周休会前获得确认，成为美国的正式司法部长。政治保护基金可能会卷土重来，爱泼斯坦档案可能会继续被掩埋。而在某个地方，罗伯特·F·肯尼迪二世正在点头同意。

先前报道：
特朗普的政治保护基金已死，长生特朗普政治保护基金
托德·布兰奇失去苏珊·柯林斯的支持票，罪魁祸首是他对反堕胎组织的秘密承诺
司法部背叛了爱泼斯坦幸存者——新墨西哥州因最新问题起诉
托德·布兰奇的确认投票被推迟，因为他拒绝将承诺写成文字
请医生佛洛伊德：托德·布兰奇在司法部长确认听证会上自称是特朗普的律师

articles.summary:
This morning started with Senator Lisa Murkowski announcing she will vote against Todd Blanche’s confirmation as Attorney General, leaving Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana as the sole remaining Republican vote standing between Blanche and confirmation… or between Blanche and the longest, most humiliating cabinet confirmation defeat since 1989.

But Cassidy has not learned a thing since being snookered by Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.

Murkowski’s statement, posted to X at 6 a.m., was characteristically measured and characteristically pointed. She said Blanche “comes across as decent and capable,” appreciated his trip to Alaska, noted several decisions she approved of, and then: “Ultimately, however, I will oppose his nomination. The politicization — even weaponization — of the Department did not start with this administration but has accelerated during it.” She cited the Epstein files, the IRS immunity granted to Trump and his family, the anti-weaponization fund, and the targeting of Trump’s political enemies. “The country needs an Attorney General who will check the worst impulses of this administration,” she wrote. “I hope Mr. Blanche is able to achieve that, if confirmed, but I simply do not have confidence that will be the case.”

With Murkowski and Collins both out, and Mitch McConnell still absent from the Senate recovering from a June fall, Blanche has exactly zero votes to spare. Cue the spotlight on Cassidy, a lame duck Republican who lost his primary to a Trump-backed challenger earlier this year and has spent the subsequent months demonstrating increasing independence from the administration that worked to end his career.

Cassidy said yes anyway. “All considered, I will vote for Mr. Blanche,” he said in a floor speech Friday morning. “I’ll be criticized for this vote. What’s new?”

In explaining his vote, Cassidy said he weighed concerns about DOJ’s “weaponization,” specifically the ongoing probe into Cassidy Hutchinson, the former White House aide and key January 6 witness, whose potential indictment has been hanging over this confirmation process like a very specific sword of Damocles. Cassidy told reporters he expressed concern about what he described as “lawfare,” prosecutions driven “not for a valid reason, but because somebody in high office is angry at them.” He is not wrong that this is a problem! …Unfortunately he’s planning on voting for the henchman enabling Donald Trump’s most vindictive streak.

We’ve seen this movie — Cassidy has absolutely been played by the administration before. He Cassidy conditioned his support for RFK Jr.’s confirmation on specific promises about vaccines, promises Kennedy proceeded to break almost immediately after being confirmed, firing the CDC’s vaccine advisory panel, cutting vaccine funding, and adding baseless content to the CDC website casting doubt on vaccine safety. Now Cassidy’s voting for Todd Blanche, who called two senators liars in his written confirmation responses, who introduced himself as Trump’s lawyer at his own hearing, who won’t commit in writing to keeping the slush fund dead in any meaningful way, and who has spent 18 months demonstrating that his primary loyalty is to one man.

Blanche will now almost certainly be confirmed before the Senate leaves for its five-week recess and become the permanent Attorney General of the United States. The slush fund will probably come back and the Epstein files will probably remain buried. And somewhere, RFK Jr. is nodding along.

articles.title: Washington Does (Mostly) Right By Students Screwed Over By Bar Exam
articles.content:
华盛顿州最高法院在雅基马会议中心NextGen考试系统崩溃后取消7月所有律师考试后，州内三所法学院院长和所有怀有同情心的人都在为约600名无处可去的考生寻求同一解决方案：学位特权。周四，华盛顿州最高法院同意这一提议，但附带了一些条件。

首先，这是一个真正的胜利。首次报名参加雅基马考试但因非自身原因无法参加的考生现在有两个选择：参加华盛顿州9月或之后的NextGen考试，或接受免除律师考试要求的豁免并通过法院命令获得律师资格。第二个选项正是华盛顿大学、西雅图大学和冈扎加大学院长向法院提出的解决方案，也是许多人一直在呼吁的。

但还有条件限制。豁免仅限首次报名者。7月之前在任何地方参加过律师考试但未通过的考生不符合资格——他们只能将申请延期到9月或2月考试，无需再次支付费用，这算是一个补救，但不是录取。而实际上完成了7月考试的考生，无法获得豁免或9月特别重考机会，只能接受他们在条件下取得的分数，如果失败则可在2027年2月免费重考一次。这里有一个细节：能够完成考试的考生是那些获得了特殊考试安排的人——坐在较小的房间里，与600人大厅不同，这些房间的带宽足以保持软件运行。因此，唯一能够完成考试的人正是那些因特殊安排而与众不同的人，而法院现在正将他们排除在救济之外。经历了崩溃的考试，因为你的房间是唯一能正常运行的，所以你被迫接受这个结果。

此外，“豁免”并不意味着“欢迎加入律师行会，这是你的资格证”。选择豁免的考生仍需在MPRE考试中取得85分或以上，通过华盛顿州法律考试，并通过品格和道德审查。选项申请需于8月14日中午前提交至华盛顿州律师协会，录取将于10月9日生效，届时7月和9月考试结果将公布。

法院详细阐述了其决策过程。事件发生后，法院与华盛顿州律师协会、国家律师协会和法院内部每日会面，讨论潜在的解决方案。任何解决方案都必须平衡各类考生的公平性，同时履行法院维护职业标准和确保律师执照程序中公众保护的职责。

法院还暗讽了过去两周的报道，指出许多公众讨论“反映的是不完整的信息，有时甚至是完全错误的”，崩溃的原因“尚未完全确定”，完整调查仍在进行。你们取消了一个完整的律师考试行政程序！当然人们会说闲话！接受批评并继续前进。

无论如何，恭喜即将加入华盛顿州律师行会的成员。你们已经有一个了不起的故事可以讲述。
articles.summary:
When Washington called off its entire July bar exam after the NextGen debut face-planted in a Yakima convention center, the state’s three law school deans and pretty much anyone with a scrap of compassion were all begging for the same answer for the roughly 600 applicants left holding nothing: diploma privilege. On Thursday, the Washington Supreme Court agreed. With some asterisks.

Start with the win, because it’s a real one. First-time applicants who were registered to take the exam in Yakima and couldn’t, through no fault of their own, now get a choice: take a Washington NextGen exam in September or later, or accept a waiver of the bar exam requirement and be admitted to the bar by order of the court. That second option is the exact remedy the deans of UW, Seattle U, and Gonzaga urged on the court, and the one some of us have been muttering about since jump.

Now the asterisks.

The waiver is only for first-timers. Applicants who had sat for a bar exam anywhere before July and failed to pass are not eligible — they get to roll their applications over to the September or February exam without paying the fees again, which is something, I guess, but it is not admission.

And then there’s the group that actually finished the July exam: no waiver, no special September do-over, just whatever score they managed under the conditions, with a fee-free February 2027 re-sit available if they fail. And here’s a wrinkle: the applicants who were able to complete the exam were those who had testing accommodations — seated in smaller rooms that, unlike the 600-person main hall, had the bandwidth to keep the software running. So the only people who got to finish were the ones an accommodation happened to separate from the crowd, and they are precisely the people the court has now shut out of relief. Grind through the broken exam, because your room was the one that worked, and you’re stuck with it.

And “waiver” does not mean “welcome to the bar, here’s your card.” Applicants who elect it still have to clear the MPRE with a score of 85 or better, pass the Washington Law Component, and survive character and fitness. Elections are due to the WSBA by noon on August 14, and admissions take effect October 9, when the July and September exam results come out.

The court was at pains to show its work. Since the incident, it wrote:

We have been meeting daily with the WSBA, the NCBE and within the Court to discuss potential resolutions. Any resolution must balance fairness to the various categories of applicants, along with the Court’s duty to uphold professional standards and ensure public protection in the lawyer licensing process.

It also took a quiet swipe at the two weeks of coverage that preceded it, noting that much of the public discussion “reflects partial information, or, in some instances, is outright incorrect,” that the causes of the failure “have not yet been fully identified,” and that a full investigation is still to come. MY DUDES — you had to cancel an entire administration of a bar exam! Of course people are going to talk shit! Take your lumps and move on.

In any event, congratulations to the soon-to-be members of the Washington bar. You have a helluva war story under your belt already.
